subsystems.name: Shade elements
subsystems.role: the individual films that block or deflect a small share of sunlight before it reaches Earth.

subsystems.name: Attitude control
subsystems.role: each element must hold its angle, because tilting a film in sunlight changes the force on it.

subsystems.name: Orbit and formation control
subsystems.role: L1 is an unstable balance point, so the whole shade must be actively held in place.

subsystems.name: Deployment structure
subsystems.role: packed films must unfold reliably after months in vacuum and temperature swings.

subsystems.name: Power and communication
subsystems.role: thousands to millions of units must be tracked and commanded, or operate autonomously.

subsystems.name: Ground segment
subsystems.role: the modelling and monitoring that measures how much sunlight is actually being blocked.

buildSteps.title: Fix the target
buildSteps.detail: Decide the fraction of incoming sunlight to remove — around 1 to 2 percent offsets a large part of accumulated greenhouse forcing — and size the shade from that.

buildSteps.title: Design the film
buildSteps.detail: Choose a material a few tens to a few hundreds of nanometres thick: a metal-coated polymer, an aluminised ceramic, or a diffractive grating film that bends light sideways instead of reflecting it back.

buildSteps.title: Mass-produce the tiles
buildSteps.detail: Roll-to-roll vacuum deposition coats and cuts film into standard panels of perhaps metres across, each weighing grams to kilograms.

buildSteps.title: Package and launch
buildSteps.detail: Panels are folded or rolled into stacks and launched to low Earth orbit; tens of millions of tonnes means either thousands of very large rockets or manufacturing off-Earth from lunar or asteroid material.

buildSteps.title: Transfer to L1
buildSteps.detail: Solar-electric or sail propulsion spirals each unit out to the Sun–Earth L1 point, about 1.5 million km sunward of Earth, over months.

buildSteps.title: Deploy and orient
buildSteps.detail: Each film unfolds and tilts to the angle where solar radiation pressure provides the small sunward push that keeps it near L1.

buildSteps.title: Build the formation
buildSteps.detail: Units spread into a sparse cloud positioned to shade Earth without colliding, each under independent control so the whole can be steered and, if needed, turned off.

buildSteps.title: Verify and tune
buildSteps.detail: Radiometers and climate models compare measured sunlight at Earth with the intended reduction, and the formation is adjusted slowly to avoid abrupt regional effects.

buildSteps.title: Plan the exit
buildSteps.detail: A design that can be dispersed or de-orbited matters, because a sudden stop would cause a rapid warming rebound.

prerequisites.tech: Large, ultra-light deployable films in space
prerequisites.why: solar sails such as Japan's IKAROS in 2010 and LightSail 2 in 2019 proved controlled deployment and solar-pressure steering, but at tens to hundreds of square metres, not square kilometres.
mass to L1 is the deciding cost; it must fall by orders of magnitude from today's prices for an Earth-launched shade to be conceivable.
the only plausible way to avoid launching tens of millions of tonnes from Earth is building the films in space from lunar or asteroid material.

prerequisites.tech: Formation flying at L1 at scale
prerequisites.why: spacecraft have held halo orbits there for decades (SOHO from 1996, ACE from 1997, DSCOVR from 2015), but no mission has coordinated a vast free-flying fleet with metre-level control.
a uniform reduction in solar flux is not a uniform change in weather — rainfall, monsoons and sea ice shift in ways models disagree on.

pathway.milestone: solar-sail and thin-film demonstrations in Earth orbit, and steady L1 operations by science spacecraft
pathway.unlocks: confidence that films can be deployed and steered, and that L1 halo orbits are routinely maintained.

pathway.milestone: a small free-flying formation at L1 — a handful of film elements holding position together for a year
pathway.unlocks: real data on attitude control, degradation and station-keeping mass budgets.

pathway.milestone: launch costs and off-Earth material processing improve by orders of magnitude
pathway.unlocks: the first shade precursors of real climatic significance, sized in the thousands of tonnes.

pathway.milestone: incremental deployment of a full-scale shade, with an agreed monitoring and shut-off regime
pathway.unlocks: a lever that could slow warming while emissions fall — if the governance and climate understanding also exist.
